St. Conláed of Kildare · St. Conlaed of Kildare · Conleth

Introduction

St. Conleth is the first bishop of Kildare, associated with St. Brigid’s monastic community and remembered in ROCOR’s official British Isles list.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Conleth, also called Conláed, was the first bishop of Kildare. The historical reference traces his early life to a hermitage near the River Liffey and attributes this account to the early Life of St. Brigid by Cogitosus.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Opening paragraph

Life and notable events

According to that Life, St. Brigid invited him to exercise episcopal ministry in her double monastery, a community including women and men. He shared in its governance. Irish genealogical traditions also describe him as a skilled metalworker. These details belong to identified medieval sources; the later claims about the reach of Kildare’s authority require their own historical context.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Cogitosus narrative and genealogical description

Death and limits of the evidence

The records place his death in either 516 or 520. A later story says that wolves killed him during a journey; the reference notes that this may be a legend connected with an explanation of his name. It should not be reported as an independently established martyrdom.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Martyrology legend and differing death records

Commemoration and legacy

The reference records the enshrinement of his relics at Kildare in the late eighth century. ROCOR’s diocesan list expressly recognizes St. Conleth among the Orthodox Saints of the British Isles.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Final paragraph on the relics · [1] Official diocesan recognition list · St Conleth, first Bishop of Kildare
